_meta.purpose: Binding university lists for the Axelis Ivy League Charter (web page + contract annex). Each list follows exactly one stated, citable definition.

gradField.true: Offers a range of master's (and usually MBA or business master's) programmes open to outside international applicants.
gradField.limited: Offers only one or a few master's programmes open to outside applicants (niche, small cohort, or eligibility-restricted); no MBA.
gradField.false: Offers no master's/MBA programme an outside international student can currently apply to (undergraduate-only, programme suspended, or open only to the institution's own undergraduates).

_meta.campusScope: Only the named main campus counts. Branch, regional, satellite, online-only and other system campuses are excluded unless named.

ivyPlus.definition: Ivy-Plus = the eight Ivy League colleges plus the University of Chicago, Duke University, MIT and Stanford University (12 colleges), as defined by Chetty, Deming & Friedman (Opportunity Insights). Listed here: the four non-Ivy members only.
ivyPlus.verbatim: "Less than half of one percent of Americans attend Ivy-Plus colleges (the eight Ivy League colleges, Chicago, Duke, MIT, and Stanford). Yet these twelve colleges account for..." (Introduction, p.1 / PDF p.2); abstract: "Ivy-Plus colleges (Ivy League, Stanford, MIT, Duke, and Chicago)".
ivyPlus.source: Chetty, R., Deming, D.J., Friedman, J.N. 'Diversifying Society's Leaders? The Determinants and Causal Effects of Admission to Highly Selective Private Colleges', NBER Working Paper 31492 (2023; revised Aug 2025). https://opportunityinsights.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/CollegeAdmissions_Paper.pdf ; https://www.nber.org/papers/w31492
ivyPlus.whyChosen: It is the admissions-research definition behind the widely reported 2023 findings on legacy/athlete preferences, so it is what the admissions press and families usually mean by 'Ivy-Plus'. It is a fixed, published, citable set of 12.

alternativeNotUsed.name: Ivy Plus Libraries Confederation (13 members)

publicIvies.definition: The 30 universities profiled in Howard R. Greene & Matthew W. Greene, The Public Ivies: America's Flagship Public Universities (New York: Cliff Street Books/HarperCollins, 2001; ISBN 0-06-093459-X). Main campus only (see _meta.campusScope).
publicIvies.source: Greene & Greene (2001), ISBN 0-06-093459-X. List as transcribed at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Ivy (section 'Greenes' Guides list (2001)') and corroborated at https://www.bestcolleges.com/blog/public-ivy-schools-and-little-ivies/ . The book itself was not inspected; the two secondary sources may not be independent.
publicIvies.whyChosen: Names individual campuses (six UC campuses explicitly), is a fixed published set of 30, and is the modern standard reference. Moll (1985) names 'University of California' as a whole system, which is ambiguous for a contract.
publicIvies.branchCampusExclusions: Excluded unless named: Rutgers–Newark and Rutgers–Camden; Penn State Commonwealth campuses (and Penn State World Campus); UW Bothell and UW Tacoma; UM-Dearborn and UM-Flint; other University of Minnesota campuses (Duluth, Morris, Rochester, Crookston); Ohio State regional campuses; UConn regional campuses; Miami University regionals (Hamilton, Middletown); other IU campuses (incl. Indianapolis); other UC, UNC, UT, SUNY and CU campuses.

littleIvies.definition: The 18 colleges shown as 'Little Ivies' in the Bloomberg Businessweek chart 'Prestige Can't Buy Performance' accompanying McDonald & Smith, 'Little Good News for the Little Ivies', Bloomberg Businessweek, 22 Dec 2016.
littleIvies.source: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-12-22/little-good-news-for-the-little-ivies (archived: https://web.archive.org/web/20170201234955/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-12-22/little-good-news-for-the-little-ivies ; chart image: https://assets.bwbx.io/images/users/iqjWHBFdfxIU/iVbPvJL9p4qs/v0/-1x-1.png). Article text: 'a group of 18 liberal arts schools sometimes dubbed "Little Ivies"'. This is the list used by https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Ivies .
littleIvies.verification: All 18 names read directly from the archived Bloomberg chart image on 2026-09-29; they match Wikipedia's list exactly.
littleIvies.whyChosen: No official body defines the Little Ivies. This is the most widely reproduced list (it is Wikipedia's list), comes from a dated, named primary publication, and is a fixed set. NESCAC-only definitions exclude Bucknell, Colgate, Lafayette, Haverford, Swarthmore, Union and Vassar and include Hamilton etc. inconsistently across sources.
